scope: Actual upload HTTP/JWT boundary, services, R2/Worker and local Redis; no full app, browser or device certification
cases: actual HTTP multipart upload requires JWT, uses a generated immutable private key and preserves original bytes
public profile media is authorized by its current profile relation and delivered by the real Worker
direct R2 PUT uses the exact signed headers and finalization rejects another user or key
eight finalizers commit one file; retries work after intent expiry and reused PUTs cannot overwrite finalized bytes
the actual image worker consumes a uniquely isolated Redis queue and publishes decodable R2 variants
actual HTTP private original and variant access deny anonymous and other-account requests
HTTP batch renewal retains the selected variant, enforces parent ownership and refuses arbitrary origins
HTML disguised as an image and truncated image bytes cannot become files; unsafe names/types cannot create upload capabilities
failed content cannot renew, revoked sessions are refused and removed profile relations stop new public capabilities
antivirus: Deferred explicitly by product owner; no malware-free claim
